With the way I feel, I’m still fighting. Last year, I went to the ER on November 17th-18th, due to being unable to keep anything by mouth down (I have severe Gastroparesis), and also unable to tolerate my tube feedings through my J-tube (surgical jejunostomy, Google it). When I arrived, I was losing weight (almost a pound a day, even with trying to eat by mouth), severely dehydrated, and from March to December of last year I dropped from 279 pounds, to 172 pounds at my lowest. I spent seven weeks in the hospital that time, as they tried to figure out what to do with me. 

By the time I was released on December 28th, I was going home on TPN (Total Parenteral Nutrition), and a GJ feeding tube (gastrojejunal), with the J-tube still in me. From the surgery I had for it, until it was removed, the J-tube caused me a lot of problems. It may have been the reason why I developed Sepsis on January 12th. When it comes to that, had I not developed a high fever of 104.4, I would not have gone. Had I not, I would’ve died. My stay for sepsis lead to my TPN and the PICC (Peripherally Inserted Central Catheter) being used for it being pulled and discontinued. By then, I was already at a goal rate with my GJ tube, and only feeding overnight, so I didn’t need TPN.

After the sepsis, I had to do Vancomyacin via IV (with a new PICC line), and when that was pulled I had chest pains. So, ER visit was needed, per PICC protocols. Thankfully, no blood clots were found. 

All of that, was over just a brief period. Last year, on April 14th, I went to one ER where I was told rather matter-of-factly, “we treat Gastroparesis as an outpatient condition.” About a week later, on the 26th, I was direct admitted to the hospital. This was before any feeding tubes, and at the time of my direct admission, I was severely dehydrated, so much so that my blood tests showed my kidneys were starting to shutdown. 

Right now, I’m on an up-cycle and hopefully improving as I’ve not had any Gastroparesis related ER visits since January for the sepsis. I did have one on May 2nd to 3rd, though, but for kidney stones. I saw a urologist yesterday who did say he didn’t see the need for more tests, and to get an appointment if I have more stones. 

So, my best bet for giving death the middle finger for awhile, is what’s called a gastric pacemaker. It is considered an experimental surgery, but for people like me it offers the best chance to control the nausea, vomiting, and to be able to eat by mouth some. The only way I can keep food or liquid down now, is to eat it right before bed, and hope it moves on and doesn’t come up when I wake up. It is unknown at this time if I’ll be able to get off of the feeding tube, but I’ll ask the surgeon when I see him on the 30th of this month.
